chunk_a.text_snippet:
Title: Can Europe’s public service media survive attacks by the far right?
Date: 2026-03-31

Content: The public broadcaster, TVP, was rocked by the changes in the run-up to Christmas in 2023, with its news channel TVP Info forced off air for more than a week and the main news bulletin given a new name to mark a break from the previous era. But Poland’s public media remains politicised within a deeply polarised media landscape. An Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe report from last year’s presidential election said the rocky transition “failed to ensure impartiality, despite some reporting improvements”. The Federation of Screenwriters in Europe said the far-right media playbook aimed to “delegitimise journalism, intimidate critics, concentrate media influence, weaponise regulators – and defund or capture public institutions that shape shared reality”. Addressing the French parliament’s inquiry last week, Bolloré denied he was waging a political war, claiming he was the “perfect scapegoat” for a hostile elite. “We do not bow,” the billionaire said. “We are free.

chunk_b.text_snippet:
Title: In Europe, lobbyists are using soaring fuel prices to make the case for more dirty energy
Date: 2026-04-01

Content: Other countries are also showing symptoms of backsliding. There are chilling signs that the Orbán media playbook is being used as a blueprint. The Italian government has used defamation suits to silence journalists and public intellectuals. In France a far-right-led parliamentary inquiry into public broadcasting has been accused by Le Monde of acting like an “ideological war machine”. In Germany, the far-right Alternative für Deutschland party has the country’s network of public broadcasters in its sights. A new series by the Guardian’s Europe correspondents gives a powerful picture of what’s happening – and why it matters. The good news is that the fightback is also under way. Until next week. initial_question.rag_input: How does the specific approach used by the AfD in Germany toward public broadcasters compare to the broader playbook described by the Federation of Screenwriters in Europe as of April 2026?
initial_question.question: How does the specific approach used by the AfD in Germany toward public broadcasters compare to the broader playbook described by the Federation of Screenwriters in Europe as of April 2026?
initial_question.answer: As of April 2026, the AfD's approach in Germany involves targeting the country's network of public broadcasters, which aligns with the 'far-right media playbook' identified by the Federation of Screenwriters in Europe. This playbook aims to delegitimise journalism, intimidate critics, concentrate media influence, weaponise regulators, and either defund or capture public institutions that shape shared reality.
initial_question.bridging_topic: Far-right influence and media institutional independence
